prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active forms that made incretin-based therapy of type 2 diabetes and obesity possible

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged from round 1: a single-part prize on B036 for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The case is about content, not the six first-place ballots. The chain runs from proglucagon processing and the biologically active GLP-1(7-36) peptide, through Holst's human incretin physiology and Drucker's work on mechanisms and tissue actions, to agonists whose benefit in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease has been confirmed in large independent randomized trials. Nobody in round 1 questioned maturity or the stability of the interpretation. On the chair's question about the third slot, I would settle it by asking which contribution is a discovery about what GLP-1 is and does. Mojsov's work on the active peptide form belongs to that discovery. Knudsen's analogue design is decisive for the drugs but is development built on it, and the citation wording can name the therapeutic consequence without crediting a person for it. I do not think a second part is justified. The three-person limit is already used by B036, so any second part would need a pair of names who cannot be accommodated. I also do not think the strength of B036 needs a second achievement to support it.
statement.case_against: The allocation remains imperfect and I do not want to hide it. Habener is outside the credited names yet has a real claim to the early proglucagon and peptide work, so the citation will honour a physiology story with a gap. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide is contested, and I cannot confirm it from the supplied evidence. If it proved untenable, the case for the Mojsov slot would weaken and Knudsen would become the better third name. A committee that weighs transformation of care equally with discovery could reasonably prefer the Knudsen version. The chair asked whether the same principle should apply to B036 as to B026, B031 and B047, where foundational work lies outside the credited names. It should, and I accept that B036 carries a version of the same weakness in the Habener omission. I judge it less severe because the credited trio covers the central physiological discovery, whereas those candidates credit a later development step.

responses.point: Linnarsson moved from Drucker, Holst and Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, but states that if the Committee values transformation of care as much as discovery, the Knudsen version would be better.
responses.response: I made the same move for the same reason, and I agree the choice depends on the criterion. I would not weigh transformation of care equally with discovery for this prize, because the clinical transformation already follows from the physiology and is acknowledged in the citation. The honest test of that choice is whether Mojsov's claim to the active peptide holds up. I cannot verify that from the evidence supplied, and neither of us can. I would therefore treat Knudsen as the substitute if the committee finds the Mojsov credit unsupportable. I would not treat it as an equal alternative.

responses.point: Perlmann supports the physiology trio, asks that Habener's absence be noted when the citation is worded, and observes that B006 cannot be combined with B036 under the three-person limit because Mori and Walter would add two names.
responses.response: The three-person arithmetic is the strongest argument against a second part, and I accept it. The limit is binding, not a drafting detail. On Habener, I would record his position in the deliberation record and keep the citation wording about the discoveries, not named people. Citing a peptide-biology claim in the wording while the credited names do not cover it would put a gap in the public text. This is the same view I took in round 1, but I now hold that the record is the right place for it, not the citation.

responses.point: The chair's round-2 questions ask whether the principle that foundational work outside the credited names weakens a candidacy (B026, B031, B047) should be applied consistently to B036, and whether a second part is wanted.
responses.response: I would apply it consistently, which is why I still rank B026, B031 and B047 below the leading position. The difference of degree matters. For B036 the credited trio contains the physiology discovery, with Habener's omission a real but partial gap. For B026 and B031 the discovery that made the drug possible lies outside the credited pair or trio. On a second part, I do not see a pairing that works under three people. I would keep B036 alone and treat B006 as the first fallback if allocation stalls, with B042 behind it.

responses.point: El-Manira regards B042 as the strongest non-GLP-1 case but notes six credited names for three places and the risk of a prize for a method. His uncertainties also ask how B042 would compare with B006 if B036 were set aside.
responses.response: I agree that B042 is the strongest case on breadth of influence among the non-GLP-1 candidates. If B036 were set aside, I would still place B006 first. Mori and Walter are the pivotal pair, the mechanism is conceptually clear and the allocation needs no cuts. B042 would require leaving out Bamberg, Boyden and Miesenböck on a discovery argument I do not find straightforward, and the tool-versus-discovery problem remains. This is a change in emphasis from round 1, where I listed B042 first, but I have not changed the alternatives themselves.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius lists B031 and B047 as alternatives and asks whether the gaps in B026 (BCR-ABL) and B047 (Eshhar) would disqualify those candidates.
responses.response: I think the Eshhar gap is a real problem for B047, because the credited three omit the person who first built a chimeric receptor for T cells. It would not disqualify the candidacy outright, but I would not bring it forward as a second part. I place B031 below B006 for the reason I gave in round 1. I take the point that its patient benefit is more direct, but the cytokine cloning and antibody engineering lie outside the pair. Neither B047 nor B031 enters my alternatives.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to the active peptide can be supported as the third B036 credit. I cannot check it from the supplied evidence, and my recollection is unverified.
Whether the Committee records Habener's position in the deliberation record or the citation. I favour the record.
Whether other members will adopt a two-part configuration. I see no workable one under the three-person limit.
The ordering of B006 and B042 as fallbacks, which depends on how the Committee treats a methods advance against a conceptual discovery with indirect clinical effect.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have documented co-authorship with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisen, and with Christopher Burge's group during my postdoc. None of these bears on a credited name for any shortlisted ballot. Shared Karolinska Institutet affiliation is not a conflict. No conflict has arisen from the round-1 exchange.
